Header: Procontarinia mateiana and Procontarinia mangicola Aam ki Midges

Prevention: Mango gall midge is spread by wind currents and long distance dispersal is through movement of infested plant material.
Source plant material only from clean, accredited suppliers and preferably source material that is certified.
Hoeing should be done under the tree canopy of mango tree followed by irrigation to kill the pupating midges in soil.
After fruit harvesting, prune trees and burn damaged branches away from orchard.
Collect and destroy fallen leaves that host the surviving stages (larvae and pupae) of midges.
Conserve the natural enemies; Procontarinia spp. infestation was drastically reduced because of increase in parasitism of
Galls caused by gall flies on mango leaf (A.M.
Monitoring: Midges are hard to monitor because mature larvae and pupae are hidden in the soil.
Adults are small and short lived, eggs are difficult to detect even under a microscope, and feeding larvae are hidden in plant tissue.
To monitor them, use traps to catch adults such as light traps, yellow sticky bands, etc.
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Use of foliar application of 2% neem extract on affected mango trees.
Use of yellow coloured card (20x20cm) with sticky material surrounded to mango tree up to 4 feet height from soil surface level from
The adult will be trapped on the cards due to sticky material.
The soil below the canopy of the plant should be covered with a plastic sheet to prevent the emergence of adults from the soil and also to prevent the dropping larvae to go into soil for pupation.
Direct Control (Chemical): Always wear impermeable gloves, long pants & long-sleeve shirts during spraying.
Change clothes and wash your hands immediately after applying pesticides.
Repeat sprays with 10 days interval during the flowering season
Soil treatments have also been used to kill carry-over population of larvae in soil under mango trees, apply by drenching
Regent/Refree 8 kg/acre) under the canopy of trees.
Spraying of 0.05% fenitrothion or 0.045% Dimethoate or 0.04% Diazinon at the bud burst stage of the inflorescence has been found effective in controlling the pest population
